title: Handley Page Halifax DG358
memorial_details: Handwritten Roll of Honour with dedicatory inscription. Above the list of names is a drawing of a Halifax Bomber and at base, there is an illustration of the tractor and trailer that carried them to their rest at Bwlch-y-ffridd on the evening of the accident.
inscription: In memory of the R.A.F. (V.R.) Airmen who died when their Halifax Aircraft crashed at Glascoed, Bwlch-y-ffridd in this Parish on 23rd January 1944. Their bodies rested at Bwlch-y-ffridd Institute on the evening of the 23rd.

sources.title: Accident Handley Page Halifax Mk V DG358

narrative: All nine men aboard were killed when it crashed in the parish of Aberhafesp, Montgomeryshire. IBCC records say the engine failed at about 20,000 feet over Wales and the aircraft descended into thick cloud, where severe icing made a wing fold and come off; the Halifax then struck its own tailplane and broke up in the air. Aviation Safety Network, quoting an accident form, gives a probable engine failure at 20,000 feet before a hailstorm, with the pilot descending into cloud that proved to be a storm. Three of the dead are fully identified so far. Sergeant Ellis Robert Gawler, the flight engineer, was 27 and is buried at Canford Magna. Sergeant John William Gibb, the navigator, was 18 and is buried in Aberdeen. Flight Sergeant John Stanley Spriggs, the air bomber, was 31 and is buried at Chester (Blacon).
